newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE, state both content with court ruling.
newsitem.headline: RWE, state both content with court ruling.

text.p: The German state of Rheinland Palatinate and RWE AG both expressed satisfaction on Thursday after the diversified utility was awarded partial damages against the state over the shutdown of a nuclear power plant.
RWE had demanded seven billion marks in damages for its initial investment, lost profits and cost of maintaining the station at Muelheim Kaerlich, near Koblenz in western Germany.

Rheinland Palatinate premier Kurt Beck, whose Social Democrats (SPD) form the main opposition in Bonn, said the decision was a victory for the state because the court ruled that RWE could not back up its full claim for damages.
"The damages (to RWE) are not quantifiable and also not that big," said Beck.
The Federal Supreme Court in Karlsruhe ruled the state should pay damages for the building and financing costs of the plant and the stoppage of business, but not for the full time of the hold-up.
The court also said RWE did not have to be compensated for lost profits. The exact level of damages is to be set by the state high court in Koblenz.
RWE also said it was not unhappy with the ruling.
"We are not dissatisfied with the judgement," said Harald Schueren, spokesman for RWE Energie AG, the energy subsidiary of RWE.

The Koblenz high court must now resolve the question of joint liability to determine the level of damages. The state government took this as a sign that the Supreme Court had passed the damages claim back to the state court.

State environment minister Klaudia Martini said the decision meant that RWE had not got what it wanted, adding that the passing of the case to the state court did not necessarily mean that damages would automatically be awarded.
But Martini said she doubted whether such large projects would continue to be taken on by the authorities without damage risk protection.
RWE said a final economic valuation of the decision could not be made until as it had not yet been seen in print.
